reasoning: The icon combines a Wi-Fi wedge (shown at low 1-bar fill) with a padlock badge, which users immediately read as Wi-Fi password or wireless network security. While originally a system status glyph for weak encrypted Wi-Fi, it serves well in a task list for the common household and office chores of changing, sharing, or securing Wi-Fi passwords, though it closely resembles a full-strength locked Wi-Fi icon.
